title: Breaking Down the Impact of the CHIPS Funding Deal for Quantum Firms
excerpt: The Commerce Department awarded $100 million CHIPS Act grants each to D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Quantinuum, while IonQ was notably excluded from...
content_html:
Key Points

  • Interested in D-Wave Quantum Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

  • The U.S. Commerce Department awarded $100 million each in CHIPS Act funding to D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Quantinuum to support domestic quantum computing development.

  • Rigetti and D-Wave benefit from the cash infusion by strengthening their balance sheets and reducing reliance on dilutive equity offerings amid rising expenses.

  • IonQ did not receive funding, likely due to unresolved regulatory issues from its SkyWater Technology acquisition, though its strong financial position may reduce the need for government support.

An influx of cash for some of the leading quantum computing companies, thanks to a research and development grant from the U.S. Department of Commerce, could have far-reaching impacts for investors even beyond the initial payout. Under the CHIPS Act, the Commerce Department will provide $100 million in funding each to D-Wave Quantum Inc. (NASDAQ: QBTS), Rigetti Computing (NYSE: RGTI), and Quantinuum (NASDAQ: QNT).

Together, these grants appear to send a message to the markets: Washington is committed to having a rigorous domestic quantum computing industry, but not every firm will receive federal support. In total, the quantum initiative promises more than $2 billion in incentives across the industry, with most of the funds going to support scaling of domestic manufacturing. Benefits of these grants are many, but it also means that investors will need to watch for government involvement as Uncle Sam takes a minority stake in many of the leading names in the industry.

→ Could Dave & Buster's Capitulation Signal the Bottom Is Finally In?

Rigetti Is One of the Biggest Beneficiaries

Rigetti may be one of the pure-play quantum firms most positively impacted by the Commerce Department's cash influx. The $100-million CHIPS award should help the company to accelerate its development of quantum hardware.

Rigetti will be able to benefit by directing this capital completely toward R&D efforts, and it is a significant cash injection indeed: the company ended last quarter with only about $541 million in cash reserves and liquid investments. This is not a paltry sum overall, but it is smaller than some of Rigetti's prominent rivals.

→ Running on Empty: 3 Energy Plays for Europe's Deep Freeze

As the company has mounting expenses—operating expenses widened to more than $30 million in the latest quarter—its cash pile has depleted, falling by close to $50 million between the end of 2025 and the end of Q2 2026. It's not yet to the point that investors may be concerned, but boosting the company's financial foundation now would be very welcome.
